title: The Ultimate Virgin Australia Seat Guide
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Inside Virgin Australia’s Boeing 737-8. Photo: Virgin Australia.
Virgin Australia operates a fleet of more than 100 Boeing 737 jets, including a mix of the 737-700, 737-800 and 737-8. Virgin’s regional subsidiary also uses newly built Embraer E190-E2 regional jets.
The airline recently completed a refurbishment program of its Boeing 737 fleet , meaning all 737s now have Virgin’s new-style Economy and Business seats.
Virgin Australia no longer uses the Airbus A320 . It has also ended its partnership with Alliance Airlines, so you’ll no longer end up on an Alliance-operated Fokker 100 when booking a Virgin Australia flight.
To give you an idea of what to expect when flying Virgin Australia, we’ve put together this guide to all Virgin Australia aircraft seats. Our guide also reveals the best and worst seats on each aircraft type.

Virgin Australia’s Boeing 737s
A Virgin Australia Boeing 737-800. Photo: David Syphers on Unsplash .
The Boeing 737 is the backbone of the Virgin Australia domestic and international short-haul fleet.
There is no seatback in-flight entertainment on Virgin’s Boeing 737s. Instead, you can stream a moderate selection of movies and TV shows to your personal electronic device.
Virgin’s 737-800s and 737-8s have Wi-Fi, and this is being rolled out now to the few remaining jets which don’t yet have it. The Boeing 737-700s do not have Wi-Fi.
Virgin Australia Boeing 737 Economy seats
Virgin Australia Boeing 737-8 Economy seats. Photo: Virgin Australia.
Virgin Australia has installed the same contoured leather seats in Economy on all the different versions of the Boeing 737 that it flies. These are configured in a 3-3 layout and have 30 inches of seat pitch, which is standard for this aircraft type.
Virgin’s Boeing 737 Economy seats recline and offer adjustable headrests, USB-A charging outlets and tablet holders.
The best Virgin Australia 737 Economy seats are the Economy X seats in rows 3, 4 and the exit row/s, which have more legroom. Economy X seats are free for Velocity Platinum and Platinum Plus members, and available for an extra charge to anyone else.
Key facts: Virgin Australia 737 Economy Class
Seat pitch: 30 inches
Seat width: 17 inches
In-flight entertainment: Streaming entertainment to your own device + paid Wi-Fi (there is no Wi-Fi on the 737-700s)
Best seats on the 737-800 and 737-8: Rows 3, 4, 14 & 15 have extra legroom
Best seats on the 737-700: Rows 3, 4, 5 & 11 have extra legroom
Seats to avoid on the 737-800 and 737-8: Seats 10A, 11A and 11F are missing windows and the seats in row 13 do not recline. The proximity to the bathrooms in the last row of Economy may also bother some people.
Seats to avoid on the 737-700: Row 7 has no windows and the seats in row 10 do not recline. The proximity to the bathrooms in the last row of Economy may also bother some people.
Virgin Australia Boeing 737 Business seats
Virgin Australia’s new Boeing 737-800 Business Class seats. Photo: Wilson McTaggart.
There are two rows of Business Class on Virgin Australia’s Boeing 737s . The leather recliner seats have 38 inches of pitch and are laid out in a 2-2 configuration.
Virgin Australia’s updated 737 Business Class seats have adjustable headrests, fold-out calf rests and a reasonable amount of recline. The tray table folds out from the armrest, and there’s a small table to rest drinks on the centre console.
There is ample legroom in both rows, but there is a bulkhead in front of row one. Many frequent flyers prefer the second row of Business as you have more space to stretch your legs out underneath the seat in front.
Row 1 of Virgin Australia’s new 737-800 Business Class. Photo: Matt Graham.
In its recent cabin refurbishments, Virgin Australia removed the cabin dividers separating Business from Economy. It is now installing shower curtains and overhead panels between rows 2 and 3 to make up for this.
There’s no longer a physical divider between Business and Economy. Photo: Matt Graham.
Key facts: Virgin Australia 737 Business Class
Seat pitch: 38 inches
Seat width: 19.5 inches
In-flight entertainment: Streaming entertainment to your own device + free Wi-Fi
Best seats: Many passengers prefer row 2 for the better legroom, but row 1 usually gets first choice of meals.
Virgin Australia Regional Airlines Embraer E190s
Virgin Australia recently introduced the Embraer E190-E2 into its regional fleet. This modern regional jet primarily operates within Western Australia.
USB-C charging outlets are available at each seat. Virgin eventually plans to offer Wi-Fi and streaming entertainment on these jets, but it is not yet available.
Virgin Australia Embraer E190-E2. Photo: Virgin Australia.
Virgin Australia E190-E2 Economy seats
In Economy Class, the E190-E2 is laid out in a nice 2-2 configuration – meaning there are no middle seats. The leather Economy seats have adjustable headrests.
The standard Economy seat pitch is 29 inches, which is a bit tight. But for those seeking a bit more legroom, Economy X seats are available.
Virgin Australia Regional Airlines Embraer E190-E2 cabin. Photo: Virgin Australia.
Key facts: Virgin Australia E190-E2 Economy Class
Seat pitch: 29 inches
Seat width: 18 inches
In-flight entertainment: No
Best seats: Rows 4, 5, 6 and 9 are Economy X seats with extra legroom
Seats to avoid: Row 26 (the last row) has no window and the seats don’t recline.
Virgin Australia E190-E2 Business seats
Virgin Australia offers similar, reclining Business Class seats on these jets to its mainline 737 product. The leather seats are reasonably wide and offer good legroom.
Key facts: Virgin Australia E190-E2 Business Class
Seat pitch: 37 inches
Seat width: 19.5 inches
In-flight entertainment: No
Best seats: 2A has exceptional legroom
